summary: The document is a non-functional, high-level brainstorming note for a food delivery mobile app. It lacks all technical specifications, user roles, business logic, security protocols, and measurable acceptance criteria. It is completely unready for engineering, design, or testing phases.

risk_factors.title: Total Absence of Security Architecture
risk_factors.description: The document explicitly states 'No security requirements' and provides no guidance on authentication, data encryption, or API protection for a system handling payments and personal data.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define comprehensive security requirements including OAuth2/OIDC for authentication, AES-256 for data at rest, TLS 1.3 for data in transit, and OWASP Top 10 compliance for the mobile and backend layers.

risk_factors.title: Undefined Data Privacy and Compliance
risk_factors.description: The app involves 'Customers' and 'Restaurants' and 'pay somehow', implying the collection of PII and financial data, yet there is no mention of GDPR, CCPA, or PCI-DSS compliance.
risk_factors.mitigation: Add a Data Privacy section detailing data retention policies, user consent mechanisms, and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance for payment processing.

risk_factors.title: Unmeasurable Performance and Operational Goals
risk_factors.description: Requirements like 'Delivery should happen fast' and 'Food ordering must be easy' are subjective and untestable, leading to potential project failure due to lack of defined SLAs.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define specific KPIs and SLAs, such as 'API response time < 200ms', 'Order confirmation within 5 seconds', and 'Delivery ETA accuracy within 10 minutes'.

risk_factors.title: Ambiguous Payment Integration
risk_factors.description: 'Customers can pay somehow' provides no technical direction for payment gateway integration, currency support, or transaction handling.
risk_factors.mitigation: Specify the payment provider (e.g., Stripe, PayPal), supported currencies, refund policies, and transaction state management logic.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Replace with specific UX/UI guidelines, accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1), and performance benchmarks.
Define specific roles (Customer, Restaurant Owner, Driver, Admin) and their respective permissions (e.g., Restaurant Owner can update menu, view orders, but cannot access other restaurants' data).
Specify notification types (push, SMS, email), triggers (order placed, driver assigned, delivered), and user preference settings.
Define initial reporting requirements (e.g., daily sales, order volume) and data schema to support future analytics, or explicitly exclude from MVP scope with a roadmap.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No specific features are defined, making it impossible to design the system architecture or database schema.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Detailed user stories for Customer (browse, order, track, pay), Restaurant (manage menu, accept orders), and Driver (accept jobs, navigate, deliver) with acceptance criteria.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: Lack of performance, scalability, and availability targets will lead to an unscalable and unreliable system.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Define target concurrency (e.g., 10,000 concurrent users), uptime (99.9%), latency, and scalability requirements.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No definition of entities (User, Order, Menu Item, Driver) or relationships, hindering database design.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Provide an Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD) and data dictionary for all core entities.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No definition of endpoints, data formats, or error handling, making frontend-backend integration impossible.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Define RESTful or GraphQL API endpoints with request/response schemas and error codes.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No guidance on how to handle failed payments, network issues, or out-of-stock items.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Define error codes, user-facing messages, and system behavior for common failure scenarios.

ai_recommendations: Completely rewrite the document using a standard requirements template (e.g., IEEE 830) with clear sections for Functional, Non-Functional, Security, and Data Requirements.
Define specific user personas and user stories with measurable acceptance criteria for each core feature (ordering, payment, tracking, management).
Engage a security architect to define the threat model and security controls, including authentication, authorization, and data encryption standards.
Establish a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) to link each business requirement to specific technical components, test cases, and acceptance criteria.
